extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media organizations, and media relations professionals seeking prepublication access to JAMA Network articles
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher-specific embargo policy describing who may receive prepublication access to JAMA Network articles, what materials are covered, permitted uses during the embargo period, timing of embargo lifts, and penalties for violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo agreement (no publication before release)
rubrics_metrics.description: JAMA Network grants prepublication access to selected members of the media who agree not to publish, broadcast, post online, or otherwise place information about embargoed content in the public domain until the time of their publication by the JAMA Network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access is conditional on agreeing to the embargo restriction; violation risks penalties (see penalties entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted activities during embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: During this embargo period individuals granted access to articles may read them, discuss their findings with the authors, and consult with other experts for the purpose of drafting reports, news stories, or other coverage for release at the time of article publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities are explicitly limited to preparation of coverage timed to the article publication; public dissemination remains prohibited until embargo lifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for embargo system
rubrics_metrics.description: The embargo is intended to give doctors and reporters full access to research before advising patients or publishing, to create a level playing field among reporters, and to minimize premature publication and economic disruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why embargoes exist (quoting ICMJE): allows careful preparation of coverage and consistency in timing of public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials covered by the embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the PDF of the full article scheduled for publication, the JAMA Network can provide images from an article. All of this material is subject to the embargo and is furnished exclusively for use in coverage of JAMA Network articles, and for no other purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any non-article use (e.g., commercial reuse, distribution outside coverage) is not permitted under the embargo; materials remain embargoed until lift time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoes vary and lift the time and day articles are published online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must monitor the stated publication time/day; embargo lift coincides with online publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible: staff reporters/writers/editors/producers
rubrics_metrics.description: JAMA Network will grant credentials to its embargoed content to reporters, writers, editors, and producers with staff credentials from newspapers, magazines, online news services, wire services, radio or television networks and stations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied requirement: demonstrable staff credentials from recognized news organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible: independent journalists and bloggers who regularly cover health topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent journalists (including bloggers) and editors who regularly cover health-related topics may be granted credentials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Individuals will be required to provide examples of recent work to demonstrate regular coverage of health-related topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible: some academic, government, or hospital media/PR representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Representatives of some academic, government, or hospital media/public relations departments may be granted credentials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access for institutional PR staff is possible but appears selective ('some'); likely evaluated case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible: unaffiliated PR, advertising, or production firms
rubrics_metrics.description: JAMA Network will not grant access to its embargoed content to public relations firms, advertising agencies, or production companies with no immediate affiliation to the authors or a specific article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access requires immediate affiliation to the author or article; third-party agencies without that link are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible: writers/editors for industry-created patient publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers/editors or other contributors for patient publications created and distributed by industry, such as pharmaceutical companies or device manufacturers, will not be granted access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patient-targeted publications produced by industry are treated as ineligible to receive embargoed materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible: industry representatives (pharma/device manufacturers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Representatives of industry including pharmaceutical companies or device manufacturers are not granted access to embargoed materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct industry representatives are explicitly excluded from prepublication access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible: financial or industry analysts
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial or industry analysts will not be granted access to embargoed content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts who might use info for market/financial purposes are excluded to minimize economic disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible: publications or websites supported by industry (including advocacy groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications or websites supported by industry, including patient advocacy groups, are not eligible for embargoed access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any outlet with industry support is treated as ineligible due to potential conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible: corporate media/public relations, advertising, or marketing departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Representatives of corporate media/public relations, advertising, or marketing departments will not be granted access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corporate communications and marketing staff are excluded regardless of corporate affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for breaking an embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: JAMA Network reviews embargo breaks on a case-by-case basis. Circumstances of the embargo violation will be evaluated before a determination is made regarding appropriate penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties may include loss of access to embargoed materials, loss of media credentials to JAMA Network events, suspension of the media outlet from receiving embargoed materials, and responsibility to reapply for access after suspension; penalties are not limited to the listed actions.
